item.title: My Fifth Reflection-Blog
item.description:
Inclusive Terminology

        by Aryan, Aman, Subh, Vedavati, & Gouramma

In this reflection blog, I will talk about my thoughts on presentatation on the topic Inclusive Terminology presentated by the group members- Aryan, Aman, Subh, Vedavati, and Gauramma. This was the last presentation of the course under unit 5 ‘Considerations for the information scientist’. So let’s begin.

Creative Topic

I found the topic very creative. The topic demonstrate the importance of word choices in our day to day life and how that can lead to inclusivity and exclusivity of different types and groups of people. I think that things like this: subtle but impactful, should not be ignored and dealt with care. This Idea only inspired some big techs to be careful about their word choice in technologies. Like some evidences the group used in their presentation slides are: master –> main, blacklist –> blocklist, manpower –> workforce. These minor things seems unimportant but plays a great role in real life in favouring some type and group of people over others.

item.title: My Fourth Reflection-Blog
item.description:
Introduction

I welcome you back in my fourth reflection blog of Unit 4. The Unit 4 was project based unit and was named ‘Projects on Communicating Information’. There were two small but interesting projects under it. The first one was creating a chatbot using typeboat and the second one was developing a dashboard using metabase. In this reflection blog, I will talk about the challenges, learnings and experiences I had while doing both of them. So stay tunned and we will walk through it together.

item.title: My Third Reflection-Blog
item.description:
Introduction

Welcome back to my third reflection blog. In this blog I will talk about my experiences during the third unit of the course- Information Science. The third unit was about Reflecting on failure. To reflect on failure we did some group projects where we dealt with some case studies and chapters from one very good book by Emy Edmondson on failure “The right kind of wrong: the science of failing well”. Actually the group project was that we had to go through the case study articles and chapters from the book and create a wiki page and then Individual Viva in front of the class. It was really interesting. I will tell you about everything in my blog ahead. So stay tuned and I will take you all through my journey.

item.title: My Second Reflection-Blog
item.description:
Introduction

I welcome you again in my second reflection blog. In this blog I will be talking about all my learnings and experiences during the Second Unit of the course. The second unit was the last unit before the mid-semester-break. For the First Unit there was not any written exams. But for the second one we had one big exam of 50 marks before we could get the mid-semester-break. So in this blog there is a lot to cover, from learnings to exams. Also, this was the unit where I struggled a lot. So stay tuned and I will take you through all my journey from start to the end of the Second Unit. Let’s begin the journey.

item.title: My First Reflection-Blog
item.description:
Introduction

This is a reflection blog where I will be reflecting back on all those learinings that I had from start of the second semester. The name of the major course that I have this semester is " Becoming a Reflective Information Scientists". As the name suggests, we in this course deal with datas, informations and try to derive usful insights and take decisions based on it. By now we are not learning any programming language this semester but I think we now are trying to build the foundations on which all the programming languages and information science courses will be grounded. I am now at the mid of this semester. As I move ahead with this course I will update all my learnings and experiences in the upcoming reflection blog.
